'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[2021 Myanmar protests]]
**Thirty-eight protesters are shot dead and 30 more are wounded by the [[Tatmadaw|military]] and [[Myanmar Police Force|police]] as protests against the [[2021 Myanmar coup d'état|February 1 coup]] continue across the [[Myanmar|country]]. A meeting of [[ASEAN]] nations called for restraint of the security forces but failed to unanimously call for the release of ousted leader [[Aung San Suu Kyi]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-56265962 (BBC News)]
*[[Vetlanda stabbing attack]]
**Seven people are wounded, three of them critically, after being attacked by a man with an [[axe]] in [[Vetlanda]], [[Sweden]]. Authorities are treating the incident as a [[terrorism in Sweden|terrorist]] attack. The perpetrator, a man in his 20s, is shot by police and arrested. [https://www.euronews.com/2021/03/03/eight-people-stabbed-in-suspected-terrorist-attack-in-sweden-say-police (Euronews)]
*[[Colombian conflict]]
**Ten [[FARC dissidents]] are killed and three others are wounded when the [[Colombian Army]] bombs a base housing them in [[Calamar, Guaviare]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/3/3/colombia-military-operation-kills-10-farc-dissidents (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Allied Democratic Forces insurgency]]
**Suspected [[Allied Democratic Forces|ADF]] militants kill eight civilians during a shooting attack at a market in Mambelenga, [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]]. ADF attacks have increased, with more than 140 people killed by the group since the beginning of the year. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-congo-security/suspected-islamists-kill-eight-in-attack-on-northeast-congo-village-market-idUSKBN2AV1X9 (Reuters)]
*[[Second Libyan Civil War]]
**The bodies of four [[Philippines|Filipinos]], an [[Austria]]n, and a [[Czech Republic|Czech]], all oil workers who were kidnapped and then murdered in [[Libya]] in 2015 by [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant in Libya|Islamic State]] terrorists, are found at a cemetery. [https://www.arabnews.com/node/1818806/world (''Arab News'')]
*Aftermath of the [[Zamfara kidnapping]]
**Three people are shot after [[Nigerian Armed Forces|armed forces]] open fire at a reunion of students, [[kidnap]]ped in [[Zamfara]] a week ago, and their parents in Jangebe, [[Nigeria]], while the parents protest the kidnapping. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-56230525 (BBC News)]
*Ten rockets hit the [[al Asad Airbase]] hosting [[United States|US]]-led coalition forces in [[Al Anbar Governorate]], [[Iraq]]. No one is directly killed or wounded by the strikes, but an American civilian contractor dies of a [[heart attack]] during the impact. [https://www.bbc.com/news/56249926 (BBC News)]
*[[Tigray War]]
**Following pressure from the international community, [[Ethiopia]] releases three reporters working for the [[BBC]], [[Agence France-Presse|AFP]], and [[Financial Times]], alongside two local news reporters and two translators, without charge. No reason was given for their arrest, and it is still unclear if four other journalists have been released. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-56263704 (BBC News)]

'''Businesses and economy'''
*[[Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]], [[Economy of Australia]]
***The [[Australia]]n [[Gross Domestic Product|GDP]] contracted 1.1% in 2020 amid restrictions related to the [[COVID-19 pandemic|pandemic]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/business/2021/mar/03/australias-economic-recovery-continues-with-31-growth-in-december-quarter (''The Guardian'')]
**[[Economy of Brazil]]
***The [[Brazil]]ian [[Gross Domestic Product|GDP]] contracts 4.1% in 2020 amid disruptions caused by the COVID-19 pandemic. It is the country's third worst economic performance after 1981 (-4.25%) and 1990 (-4.35%). [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20210303-brazil-ends-new-lost-decade-with-gdp-drop-of-4-1-in-2020 (France 24)]
*[[March 2021 United Kingdom budget|2021 United Kingdom budget]]
**[[Chancellor of the Exchequer]] [[Rishi Sunak]] delivers the 2021 Spring [[Budget of the United Kingdom|budget]] to the [[House of Commons of the United Kingdom|House of Commons]], announcing the [[government of the United Kingdom|government]]'s tax and spending plans for the year ahead, as well as further [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom|COVID-19]] support measures, including extending the [[furlough]] until the end of September and increasing the [[minimum wage]] beginning in April. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-politics-56266773 (BBC News)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*Ten people are killed in a [[plane crash]] in [[Jonglei State]], [[South Sudan]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/3/3/10-killed-in-south-sudan-plane-crash-governor (Al Jazeera)]
*A 6.3 magnitude [[list of earthquakes in Greece|earthquake]] strikes central [[Greece]] and is felt in neighbouring countries. Most of the damage is reported in the [[Greek region]] of [[Thessaly]]. [https://apnews.com/article/europe-kosovo-montenegro-earthquakes-greece-5cbaa10cebbbad65964966b7a276420c (AP News)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
****[[COVID-19 vaccination in India]]
*****[[President of India|President]] [[Ram Nath Kovind]] receives his first dose of the [[COVID-19 vaccine]]. [https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/president-kovind-receives-first-dose-of-covid-19-vaccine-at-delhi-s-rr-hospital-101614758862461.html (''Hindustan Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Taiwan]]
****[[Taiwan]] receives their first shipment of the [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|Oxford–AstraZeneca]] [[vaccine]] through the [[COVAX]] vaccine-sharing initiative. [https://focustaiwan.tw/society/202103030005 (Focus Taiwan)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Uzbekistan]]
****[[Uzbekistan]] surpasses 80,000 cases of COVID-19. [https://m.akipress.com/news:655174:Uzbekistan_passes_80,000_coronavirus_cases/ (AKIPress)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Andorra]]
****The [[government of Andorra|government]] announces that they will receive 3,000 doses of the [[AstraZeneca]] vaccine from [[France]]. [https://www.diariandorra.ad/noticies/nacional/2021/03/03/andorra_rep_dema_000_dosis_vacuna_astrazeneca_175840_1125.html (''Diari d'Andorra'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Denmark]], [[Lineage P.1]]
****[[Denmark]] reports its first case of the Lineage P.1 variant first detected in [[Brazil]] in a person from the [[Capital Region of Denmark|Capital Region]]. [https://cphpost.dk/?p=122700 (CPH Post)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Montenegro]]
****[[Montenegro]] receives 30,000 doses of the [[Sinopharm (company)|Sinopharm]] [[Sinopharm BIBP COVID-19 vaccine|BBIBP-CorV]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] donated by [[China]]. [https://seenews.com/news/montenegro-receives-30000-doses-of-chinas-covid-19-vaccine-733151 (See News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Poland]]
****[[Poland|Polish]] biotechnology company Mabion S.A. signs an agreement with [[Novavax]] to begin commercial-scale production trials for Novavax's future [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]]. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-03-03/novavax-deal-with-mabion-boosts-poland-s-nascent-biotech-scene?srnd=premium (Bloomberg)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Slovakia]]
****[[Slovakia]] imposes an overnight curfew from 8:00 p.m. to 5:00 a.m. local time, in an attempt to reduce the spread of [[COVID-19]]. The curfew will last until at least March 19. [https://medicalxpress.com/news/2021-03-slovakia-imposes-overnight-curfew-covid.html (MedicalXpress)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Spain]]
****The [[Government of Catalonia]] announces that 79,000 vaccinated persons were mistakenly recorded as COVID-19 cases. [https://www.elperiodico.com/es/sanidad/20210302/catalunya-genera-nuevo-caos-estadistico-80000-contagios-menos-11554410 (''El Periódico'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Africa]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Rwanda]]
****[[Rwanda]] receives its first shipment of 240,000 doses of the [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|Oxford–AstraZeneca]] [[vaccine]] manufactured by the [[Serum Institute of India]] through the [[COVAX]] vaccine-sharing initiative. [https://www.newtimes.co.rw/news/photos-rwanda-receives-first-covid-19-vaccine-covax-programme (''New Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Senegal]]
****[[Senegal]] receives 324,000 doses of the Oxford–AstraZeneca [[vaccine]] through the COVAX vaccine-sharing initiative. [https://www.reuters.com/article/health-coronavirus-senegal-vaccination/senegal-receives-its-first-astrazeneca-vaccines-under-covax-idUSL5N2L12S1 (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Sudan]]
****[[Sudan]] receives over 800,000 doses of the [[University of Oxford|Oxford]]–[[AstraZeneca]] [[vaccine]] at the [[Khartoum International Airport]] through the COVAX vaccine-sharing initiative, becoming the first country in the [[Middle East and North Africa]] to receive it. [https://www.unicef.org/press-releases/sudan-receives-first-delivery-covid-19-vaccines-over-800000-doses (UNICEF)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in New Jersey]], [[variants of SARS-CoV-2]]
****[[New Jersey]] reports its first two cases of the [[Lineage P.1]] variant in [[Hudson County, New Jersey|Hudson County]] and 34 cases of a [[New York (state)|New York]] variant of [[SARS-CoV-2]] in the northeastern part of the state. [https://www.nj.com/coronavirus/2021/03/nj-confirms-2-more-highly-contagious-covid-variants-2-case-of-brazilian-and-34-cases-of-ny-variants.html (NJ.com)] 
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil]]
***[[List of Governors of São Paulo|São Paulo governor]] [[João Doria]] announces that the entire [[São Paulo (state)|state]] will revert to "red phase" restrictions, which means that all malls and non-essential businesses will be closed for two weeks beginning March 6 in order to reduce the spread of COVID-19. [https://riotimesonline.com/brazil-news/sao-paulo/sao-paulo-reverts-to-strictest-quarantine-phase-after-hospitalizing-one-person-every-two-minutes/ (''The Rio Times'')]
*[[China]] confirms an outbreak of [[African swine fever]] in [[domestic pig]]s being illegally transported through [[Funing County, Yunnan|Funing County]] in [[Yunnan]] [[provinces of China|province]]. [https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/east-asia/china-confirms-swine-fever-in-piglets-in-yunnan-province (''The Straits Times'')] 

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2021 Australian Parliament rape scandals]]
**[[Attorney-General of Australia|Attorney-General]], [[Leader of the House (Australia)|House Leader]], and [[Minister for Industrial Relations (Australia)|Industrial Relations Minister]] [[Christian Porter]] comes forward as the minister accused of [[raping]] a woman in 1988, who has since committed [[suicide]], in an anonymous letter sent to [[Prime Minister of Australia|Prime Minister]] [[Scott Morrison]] last week. Porter denies the allegations and announces that he will be taking a mental health leave. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2021-03-03/christian-porter-denies-historical-rape-allegation/13206972 (ABC Australia)]
*[[2018 Toronto van attack]]
**Alek Minassian is found guilty of [[murder]]ing 10 people, and attempting to kill 16 more, in a [[vehicle-ramming attack]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-canada-crime-van-attack-idUSKBN2AV20K (Reuters)]
*[[Aftermath of the 2021 storming of the United States Capitol]]
**The [[United States Capitol Police]] announces that it has obtained intelligence on a "possible plot" by an identified militia group to breach the [[United States Capitol]] building on the following day, March 4, which has recently been the subject of [[QAnon]] [[conspiracy theories]]. In response to the intelligence, the [[United States House of Representatives]] announces that it has ended its work for the week. [https://apnews.com/article/police-uncover-possible-plot-militia-breach-capitol-c470dc642d9b568238f80b5822787159 (AP)]
*A [[pipe bomb]] explodes outside a [[COVID-19]] test centre in [[Bovenkarspel]], [[Netherlands]], causing minor damage. No one is wounded in the explosion. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/3/3/blast-targeting-netherlands-covid-19 (Al Jazeera)]
*[[France]] bans [[Far-right politics|far-right]] [[Identitarian movement|Identitarian]] [[Nationalism|nationalist]] group [[Les Identitaires|Génération Identitaire]]. [[Interior Minister (France)|Interior Minister]] [[Gérald Darmanin]] says the movement incites "discrimination, hatred and violence". [https://www.france24.com/en/france/20210303-france-bans-far-right-anti-migrant-group-generation-identity (France 24)]
*[[Germany|German]] intelligence agency [[Federal Office for the Protection of the Constitution]] formally places [[Far-right politics in Germany (1945–present)|far-right]] oppositional party [[Alternative for Germany]] under surveillance, accusing it of aiming to subvert [[Basic Law for the Federal Republic of Germany|the constitution]]. It is the first time that a major political party has been placed under surveillance since the end of [[World War II]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/2021/03/03/world/europe/germany-afd-surveillance-extremism.html (''The New York Times'')]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Freedom House]], in its annual ''[[Freedom in the World]]'' report, downgrades [[India]] from "free" to "partially free". The report cites the [[Violence against Muslims in India|rise in mob violence against Muslims]], increased [[government of India|government]] interference in [[Judiciary of India|the judiciary]], increased intimidation against journalists and activists, and the government's heavy-handed approach to [[COVID-19 lockdown in India|COVID-19 lockdowns]] that left [[Indian migrant workers during the COVID-19 pandemic|millions of migrants stranded]] as the main reasons for the downgrade. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20210303-freedom-house-downgrades-india-to-partly-free (France 24)] [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-india-56249596 (BBC News)]
*[[Hungary]]'s ruling party [[Fidesz]] withdraws from the conservative [[European Parliament]] bloc [[European People's Party]] (EPP), after the EPP changed its rules to allow it to expel a party's entire delegation. Fidesz's membership had been suspended since 2019 after it accused then-[[President of the European Commission|European Commission President]] [[Jean-Claude Juncker]] and [[philanthropist]] [[George Soros]] of conspiring to "flood" Europe with migrants during a national campaign. [https://www.dw.com/en/hungarys-orban-pulls-fidesz-from-center-right-eu-alliance/a-56760505 (DW)]
